newsitem.title: USA: Dow extends gains as bonds firm, NYSE sets curbs.
newsitem.headline: Dow extends gains as bonds firm, NYSE sets curbs.

text.p: The Dow industrials extended gains in light afternoon trade Monday, strengthened by bonds as markets awaited a slew of economic data this week.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average was up 55 points to 8168 in thin volume. The New York Stock Exchange imposed curbs on index-arbitrage trading at 1350 EDT/1750 GMT.
The Nasdaq composite, which had been soft much of the morning, was near unchanged, up 0.44 point at 1570.
The long bond gained 16/32 to yield 6.42 percent.

"Bonds are up about half a point, and this is just a continuation of the strong market," said Guy Truicko, a portfolio manager at Unity Management. "But volume is light. The market is waiting for the data due out this week."
A strong dollar, which encouraged foreign buying of U.S. assets, technical factors and hopes for a federal budget deal were seen bolstering bonds.
Both stocks and bonds awaited the week's economic data, which include the second quarter employment cost index on Tuesday and the July employment report on Friday.
